pr_title: Fix long latencies in `ReaderWriterLockSlim` lock operations due to `Sleep(1)`
pr_body:
- Removed usage of `Sleep(1)`
- Modified the spin-waiting scheme beyond the `Sleep(0)` threshold to avoid potentially long sequences of ineffective `Sleep(0)`s
- Retuned the threshold to reprioritize deprioritized spin-lock requests

Fixes https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/69206

On the test case in the fixed issue, the output is mostly empty (no latency higher than 0.5 ms), with the occasional ~1 ms latency. There is some tradeoff in throughput when there is high contention on the spin-lock, in favor of avoiding very high latencies, with this change. It seems like a necessary and reasonable tradeoff, since the higher throughput in the baseline is mainly artificial due to the `Sleep(1)` removing many threads from the contention (and introducing high latency on those threads).

issue_context.title: There may be unexpectedly high delays in `ReaderWriterLockSlim` operations
comments:
> depending on how much contention there is

More relevant, depending on the scheduling frequency.  ~15m/s is the normal timer resolution/frequency on Windows and a bunch of other OSes.  There are ways to get faster ones, but they require additional setup, and in any case the point of a spin-lock is for things that are barely contested; if a spin-lock actually needs to wait, the longer duration is probably worth it.

review_comments:
> Avoid using only Sleep(0), as it may be ineffective when there are no other threads waiting to run.

On a single processor, this will just use Thread.Sleep(0)... is that ok?
On a single processor that's what is done elsewhere, it's unlikely that a meaningful change would occur while spin-waiting without yielding.
